job: Job 2 - On-site Inspection, full job to clearance
summary: Attic. Inspection -> estimate -> remediation -> clearance report -> paid in full
service: Scope of Work Assessment (short on-site visit to price the work)
property: 31 Ross St E, Smiths Falls, ON (house, out-of-town area)
client_concern: A home inspector found visible traces of mold, probably in the attic. Booking note: 'Visible traces of mold found by home inspector. They think it is attic in question.' The client later said they are selling the house.

timeline.what: Client support (Natasa) books a 'SoW - OOT' visit (Scope of Work, $95 + tax) for Sep 3, 2-3 PM.
Inspector visits the house: attic, thermal camera, moisture meter, hygrometer.

Inspector posts: 'Please send an invoice for $95 + tax', a note about the client expecting a 3-5 h full home inspection for a $95 service, report bullets, 18 photos with captions, and the estimate ($2,700 + tax, 6-8 h). Office replies 'GOOD TO GO!'.
Invoice MU767 ($107.35) and estimate MO994 created. Report written and reviewed the same day. Asana card created automatically at 16:43.
'Report and estimate prepared, awaiting payment.' Client pays the $107.35 invoice, then the report and estimate are sent.
Client asks if we can also check two other attic areas. Answer: yes, the crew will look while on site; extra work would get a separate estimate.
After a follow-up SMS the client replies: 'Yes, we would like MB to remediate the mold issue... How should we proceed?' Support asks them to click Accept on the estimate.
Estimate accepted. 40% booking deposit ($1,080) paid. Card moves to 'Active Projects'.
Email 'Your project is booked - optional add-ons'. SMS offers Whole-Home Treatment for $600 + tax (or $850 later). Client: 'Not useful to us, as we are selling the house'.
Crew does the attic job. Supervisor takes swab tests; instant swab negative; clearance grade 4 (best).
Project Clearance Report (20 photos: before, during, after) and the final invoice are sent. Card tagged PROJECT COMPLETED.
Final invoice paid ($3,051 total). Automated SMS asks for a Google review. Second review SMS on Oct 1.

findings: Attic: visible discoloration, no rot or structural damage, no moisture problems.
Only one layer of fiber batt insulation; some soffits blocked by insulation.
Thermal camera: uneven, disturbed insulation on the ceilings and at the attic hatch.
Popcorn ceiling that may contain asbestos, with several exposed holes.
recommendations: Bring attic insulation to R-50 and spread it evenly
Unblock soffits, add baffles for airflow
Contain the holes in the popcorn ceiling until asbestos testing

estimate_summary.status: Accepted Sep 15, invoiced (MU815), paid in full Sep 24
scope: Attic job, main attic about 600 sq ft, hard to access, fiber batt insulation
Containment at the attic hatch, negative pressure if possible
Wire-brushing + HEPA vacuum + stain remover on sheathing and trusses; remove bad insulation as needed
HEPA vacuum + fogging with fungicide, air scrubber for odors

estimate_items_from_freshbooks.description:
The inspector who prepared this estimate is:
Luka Markovic, MSC ME, CMI

Got questions? Contact Luka by phone at: 343-600-3453, or by email: luka@bustmold.com

-- Containment of the attic entrance area using polyethylene sheets, negative pressure (or an equivalent method, If permitted by actual conditions at the property) in order to help prevent any cross contamination from occurring during the removal process.

- All personal belongings should be relocated away from the attic hatch by the owner prior to the remediation process. This should be done in order for the Mold Busters remediation team to be able to bring in the necessary equipment.

-- Removal of mold from the attic area (sheathing, trusses, etc.) by means of manual wirebrushing, or other topical and abrasive removal techniques. This process is conducted alongside HEPA vacuuming, provided that conditions such as the size of the attic hatch or attic height allow for it. Additionally, we apply concentrated hydrogen peroxide or other approved fungal stain-removing agents to heavily contaminated building materials within the attic space.
Residual non-fungal staining may be present upon completion.

Portions of affected or compromised insulation may be removed and disposed of, on an as-needed basis. Any remaining insulation will be thoroughly disinfected using a fungicide.

Mold Busters' trained mold removal professionals are recommend to wear the appropriate PPE, and to complete the tasks in accordance to mold removal guidelines - https://iaq.is/mold-removal-guidelines

 Price includes equipment, materials and labor fees.

Any additional items and areas that require mold removal are subject to revision and discussion with the client.

-- Disinfection

Thorough HEPA vacuuming is conducted throughout all surfaces in the affected attic area in order to remove spores, particulates, dust, and additional debris, if conditions such as the size of the attic hatch or attic height permit.

Thorough disinfection on all surfaces, including insulation, will be performed by means of concentrated fogging with a fungicide.

All remaining materials and atmosphere in the attic area will be oxidized in order to remove any residual spores, bacteria, and additional particles. An air scrubber will be deployed in the contained attic entrance area to assist in removing residual odors from products utilized during the treatment process. Residual odors may remain for up to 48-hours, depending on the quality of ventilation within the treated space.

-- Clearance

Post-remediation verification is conducted to ensure that the environment is suitable for re-occupancy. 

The final clearance inspection includes a visual inspection, and surface swab testing of the affected area. 

This will be performed by the Project Supervisor upon completion of the remediation process.

A written report following the remediation process, describing the outcome of the remediation work, any potential source issues, clearance grades, etc.

Additional recommendations will be made in this report to assist in preventing future fungal contamination.
